name: Terminal ASCII
summary: The world drawn entirely in text glyphs on a green phosphor CRT: one fixed character grid, glowing multi-glyph figures, scanlines.
description: Everything on screen is a character in one fixed grid of 6 × 10-unit cells: meadows are sparse dim ticks (. , ' " `), forests are fields of club and spade glyphs, water is ~ and ≈, hills are ░▒▓█ density ramps and rooms are # walls around dotted floors. Figures are small multi-glyph sprites on opaque cell plates – an @-headed adventurer in amber, (ö) critters, flickering (*) spirits and a block-letter brute in red – that erase the ground under them and glow like hot phosphor. Effects are glyph bursts, rings of characters, box-drawing frames and typed-out text; the picture sits behind scanlines, a breathing flicker, a rolling refresh band and a barrel vignette with rounded glass corners.
bestFor: rapid prototypes with no art budget
avoidFor: designs that need detailed faces or many similar figure types

difficulty.why: New assets are two short text grids per sprite (glyph rows + colour-key rows) baked by one shared routine, so a new figure or prop takes minutes. The skill is ASCII-art composition: readable silhouettes in 3–7 cells, choosing glyphs by shape, and keeping the palette discipline (green world, amber main character, cyan/red as signals). The engine part (glyph atlas, character ROM for block/box glyphs, cell snapping) is written once.

technique.renderer: Canvas 2D (procedural, glyph atlas, no image assets)
technique.resolution: Full display resolution. 1 world unit = screenH / 360 px (2.5 px at 900 px). A cell is 6 × 10 units (15 × 25 px at 900 px), so the screen is 36 text rows tall. Ground chunks are 240 units (40 × 24 cells) baked at min(scale, 4) px per unit.
technique.summary: Every glyph is baked once into a glyph atlas per cell size (slot = glyph + colour + mode: plain, glow, inverse) and blitted cell by cell; block, shade and box-drawing glyphs and a few symbols (♣ ♠ ◆ ≈ ▲ ♥ ☼) are drawn procedurally like a character ROM so they tile seamlessly. Ground, figures, props, effects and numbers all snap to whole cells; only the camera scrolls smoothly.
technique.linework: No outlines. Shapes are glyph strokes of VT323 at 1.25 × cell height, double-struck (drawn twice, shifted max(1 px, 10 % of the cell width) to the right) for figures, props and effects; ground glyphs are single-struck. Box-drawing lines are max(1, round(0.15 × cell width)) px thick, double lines are two strokes 20 % of the cell width apart.
technique.shading: None inside a glyph. Volume and density come from glyph choice: the shade ramp ░ (25 % dots) ▒ (50 % checker) ▓ (75 %) █ (solid) on dot lattices of max(1, round(cellH / 12)) px, half blocks ▀ ▄ for rounded silhouettes, and brightness steps of the phosphor ramps (7 greens, 6 ambers, 5 cyans, 4 reds).
technique.lighting: Light is phosphor glow: every bright glyph is baked with a wide bloom (shadowBlur 1.0 × cell height at 75 % alpha) plus a tight halo (0.3 × cell height). Only light-emitting keys glow on props (tree tips, LEDs, sign text, fire). Warm additive radial pools (amber #ffb238, 50 % alpha, 46-unit radius) sit under campfires, and a faint 16 % amber lamp glow (52 units) under the main character.
technique.texture: The grid itself: sparse hashed glyphs per cell, dot-lattice shade glyphs, display-resolution scanlines. No noise texture is ever drawn as pixels.

paletteRules: Phosphor green carries ~90 % of the picture; the ground never goes brighter than #2a994b except room walls and tree tips.
Amber belongs to the main character, light sources and warm materials (wood, sand, roads) – no creature is amber.
Cyan and red are signal colours: cyan for collectibles, spirits, water and glow-up; red only for the large creature, small-creature eyes, errors and alerts.
Every colour family is a brightness ramp; fading = stepping one level darker per frame band, never alpha.
Cell backgrounds are near-black tints of their material (water, room, forest, road), never mid tones.
Inverse video (lit cell, dark glyph) is the only flash: fill the plate with the brightest step of the figure's family.

typography.role: All glyphs in the world, HUD numbers, titles, card titles, labels
typography.css: font: 52px/0.95 'VT323', monospace; letter-spacing: 2px; color: #a3ffbd; text-shadow: 0 0 6px rgba(77,219,118,.75), 0 0 16px rgba(77,219,118,.25);

typography.role: Small body text: card descriptions, captions, hints
typography.css: font: 500 11px/1.4 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; letter-spacing: 3px; text-transform: uppercase; color: #2a994b;

world.summary: A field of glyph cells: one hashed glyph per 6 × 10-unit cell, picked by material from noise fields. Dim green ticks for meadows, clubs and spades for forests, ~ ≈ for water on dark-teal cells, ░▒▓█ ramps for hills, dotted amber dirt roads, = bridges and rogue-style rooms with # or double-line ═║ walls, dotted floors and + doors. Water crests travel as brighter ~ ≈ glyphs every frame.
layers: Base: screen black #020a05; chunk = 240 units = 40 × 24 cells, painted from a one-cell margin so glyph overflow never seams

Material per cell (priority): room (cell-aligned rectangle 11–19 × 7–11 cells, at most one per 44 × 30-cell region, 42 % chance) > water (warped noise < 0.335; deep < 0.265) > road (distance to two noise curves < 8 units) > hill (fbm > 0.665) > forest (warped noise > 0.54) > grass
Cell backgrounds: water #031a1e / deep #042229, rooms #071f0f, dense forest #04170c, roads and bridges #0e0d05

Glyphs: grass 4–44 % density (by meadow noise) of . , ' ` " ; in #113d20/#1a6331 – large calm areas outside meadows; meadow patches " , ; in #1a6331/#2a994b; flowers only in small beds inside meadows (4 × 2-cell patches, 12 % of them, 30 % of their cells): amber * or red ♦ per bed; forest 8–48 % ♣ ♠ ^; hills ░ ▒ ▓ (12 % ▲ peaks) then █ cores; water ~ (shallow, 50 %) and ≈ (deep, 42 %); shore band . , · in amber dark; roads · centre and . , ' edges in amber dark; bridges = in amber
Rooms: walls # (#2a994b, 20 % #4ddb76; 13 % ruined into ▒ or ,) or double-line ╔═╗║╚╝, floors . in #1a6331, 2–3 doors + in amber #c97f19
Per frame: water crests where sin(0.42·col + 1.1·row − 1.9·t + 1.4·sin(0.7·row + 0.6·t)) > 0.9 – ~ in #1fb0b9, top 2.5 % as glowing ≈ in #5cefff
Per frame: additive amber light pools under campfires

characters.summary: Multi-glyph sprites, 1–7 cells wide, snapped to whole cells, each cell on an opaque plate so the figure erases the ground; every state is a designed glyph pose. Main character: a 3 × 3 '@' adventurer – white-amber @ head with a trailing scarf glyph (~ - , ` =) behind it, amber /█\ arms and torso, legs – with 16 held poses (8 walk, 4 breathing idle, blink, dash crouch, dash lunge, hurt), standing on a blinking amber ▁ cursor. Small creature: a 3 × 2 critter (ö) or {x} in two designs with 4 scuttle poses, a per-actor blink and an (×) / {#} hit pose. Fast creature: a 3 × 1 spirit flickering through (*) {+} (×) <*> {x} (+) at 11 fps with a trail of the cells it just left. Large creature: a 7 × 4 block-letter brute (▀▄█) whose horns pump, jaw chomps (vvv / VVV), eyes blink (O / -) and widen to × when hit.
rules: One glyph per cell, one colour key per cell; '.' leaves the ground visible, 'K' is a plate with no glyph
Bold = double strike: every figure glyph is drawn twice, one font pixel apart
Bake order per sprite: plates, wide bloom (blur 1.0 × cell height, 75 % alpha), tight halo (0.3 ×), crisp glyphs
Facing = mirrored glyph rows with paired glyphs swapped (/ ↔ \, ( ↔ ), < ↔ >, [ ↔ ], { ↔ }, ▌ ↔ ▐)
Feet anchor: the bottom row of the sprite sits in the cell that holds the figure's y; column = round(x / 6 − width / 2)
Flash = inverse video (plate lit in the family's brightest colour, glyphs in plate black) while flash > 0.45
Materialise: cells type in one by one between 25 % and 90 % of the appear time, earlier cells show scrambling noise glyphs from #%&$@?!*+=/<>{}[]~^:;░▒▓
Dissolve: each cell drifts 1.5–4 cells its own way and decays ▓ ▒ ░ · . while stepping down its colour ramp

Hit on the main character: the hurt pose (head X, arms up) with 55 % of its cells scrambling to red noise glyphs for ~0.18 s; dash = a crouch pose for 45 ms, then the lunge (scarf =, arms -█=, legs / >) leaving ▓ ▒ ░ afterimages in amber
Creatures switch to their hit pose while flash > 0.25 and are knocked one whole cell in the push direction while flash > 0.55; the dissolve starts from the hit pose.

Secondary motion in glyphs: the scarf cell changes one pose behind the legs (~ ~ - -), idle swaps arms /█\ → |█| on the exhale; blinks swap a single glyph (@ → o, ö → -, O → -) on each actor's own timer.

props.summary: Glyph-art objects on plates, snapped to cells and y-sorted with the figures: 5 × 6 stacked-^ pines with a ║ trunk, 6 × 4 (&&&&) oaks, 4 × 2 bushes, 6 × 3 outlined boulders with ░▒▓ shading, a 3 × 5 half-block monolith with a blinking cyan ■ LED, a box-drawing signpost with a blinking >_ prompt, # ruin walls, a flickering campfire )▲( on =#= logs, a cyan > stairs glyph and an amber [=] chest inside rooms.
rules: Same sprite format as figures: glyph rows + colour-key rows, plates behind every non-'.' cell
Only light-emitting keys bloom (tree tips, LEDs, sign text, fire, stairs); stone, wood and foliage are drawn without glow
Props stay in the green family (#1a6331–#4ddb76) with amber only for wood, fire and treasure
Animated props swap whole glyph rows: fire 4 frames at 7 fps, LED 2-on-1-off at 1.4 Hz, sign cursor 1.06 s blink, stairs pulse
A tree that a figure stands behind is redrawn without plates and dimmed one step so the figure shows through
Rooms get furniture from their own seed: a campfire in the middle (60 %), stairs (55 %), a chest (60 %), a monolith (40 %)

effects.name: Glyph burst
effects.how: Impacts throw 2 glyphs from * + ' ` in the struck figure's colour family; bursts throw 6 (16 for the large creature) of the figure's own glyphs plus 3–8 * + x. Each particle is one glyph snapped to the cell grid, decaying to · and . (shade glyphs to ▒ ░) in its last 45 % while stepping down its colour ramp.

effects.name: Glyph ring
effects.how: A ring of * (# for the large creature) on the cell grid, radius growing 4 → 22 units (46 for large) with ease-out over 0.32–0.55 s, y squashed to 0.6, glyphs dedupe per cell and turn to · after 60 % of their life.

effects.name: Ash residue
effects.how: Where a figure dissolved, 4 (large: 9) cells of shade glyphs stay on the ground and decay ▒ → ░ → · → . over 1.1–1.6 s in the figure's darkest colours, each cell vanishing at its own moment.

effects.name: Box frame glow-up
effects.how: A box-drawing frame ┌─┐│└┘ in cyan growing from 1 to 6 cells half-height around the main character over 0.7 s, plus the typed text [ OK ] above and ten rising ↑ ▲ glyphs in cyan and amber.

effects.name: Typed-out text
effects.how: Short words (OK, ERR, SIGNAL LOST) appear one character per cell over the first 30 % of their life with a blinking █ cursor at the end, then scramble into noise glyphs in the last 25 %.

effects.name: Collectibles and spinner
effects.how: Small collectibles are a single cyan ◆ on a plate that blinks to ◇ one frame in five; large ones are [◆]. The orbiting object is a terminal spinner | / - \ at 12 fps in white-amber between amber ( ) brackets, with a fading · on its previous spot.

effects.name: Projectile
effects.how: A white-amber * on a plate with up to two trail cells behind it: the direction glyph - \ | / (by angle, 45° steps) in amber and a dim ·.

effects.name: Row tearing
effects.how: On heavy impacts 2–5 horizontal strips, each 1–3 text rows tall and aligned to the text rows, slide sideways by up to two whole cells and settle back over 0.14–0.5 s.

atmosphere.summary: A CRT tube: baked phosphor bloom on every bright glyph, display-resolution scanlines, a breathing flicker, a slow rolling refresh band, a barrel vignette with darker edges and rounded black glass corners, a faint glass reflection, and row tearing on impacts. No shadows – figures stand on cells, the main character on a blinking cursor.
rules: Bloom is baked into the glyph atlas and sprites (two shadow-blur passes), never computed full-screen per frame
Scanlines: every max(3, round(screenH / 300)) display px a dark row of a third of that height at rgba(0,0,0,0.42)
Flicker: a black veil of 1.2–6.2 % alpha – hashed noise changing 30 times per second plus a slow swell (sin 1.7 t)
Rolling band: an additive green gradient 14 % of the screen tall at 3.5 % alpha, sweeping down every 9.8 s
Vignette: radial black 0 → 16 % (55 %) → 50 % (85 %) → 82 % at the corners, 6 % edge bands at 55 %, rounded screen corners of 7.5 % of the short side
Glass reflection: a soft radial highlight rgba(200,255,220,0.045) at the upper left
Shadows do not exist: the main character's cell below is a ▁ cursor blinking with a 1.06 s period

ui.summary: Terminal windows: near-black panels with a 2-px #2a994b frame, a black outer ring and a soft green glow, scanline texture, and a title cut into the top border like a legend (PWR in amber). Bars are block segments (8 px block, 2 px gap) in bright green or amber with a drop-shadow glow over a dim segmented track. Big numbers in VT323 with phosphor text-shadow; captions in IBM Plex Mono with a > or $ prompt; blinking █ and _ cursors; cards have a lit title strip with [1] keys and switch to amber with an inverse-video title on hover.

motion: Everything moves in whole cells (6 units across, 10 down); only the camera scrolls smoothly – movement reads as discrete terminal steps.

Main character: 8 held walk poses at anim × 0.9 (legs / \ → /| → | → |\ …, arms /█\ -█\ |█| /█- counter-swinging, scarf ~ ~ - - lagging one pose); idle: 4 breathing poses 0.5 s each + a blink pose (@ → o) for 0.16 s every 3.6 s; while firing, the arm on the facing side turns into - / \ | toward the aim.
Dash: crouch pose (<█ over /_\) for the first 45 ms as anticipation, then the lunge pose with amber ▓ ▒ ░ afterimages; hurt pose while hurtT > 0.45.

Small creature: 4 scuttle poses at anim × 1.6 + seed (legs /"\ |"| \"/ |"|), blink 5 % of a 3 s cycle with its own phase; large creature: 4 stomp poses at anim × 1.0 (horns ▀▄ ↔ ▄▀, jaw vvv ↔ VVV, feet swap) with its own blink.
Fast creature: glyph flicker through 6 bracket/core combinations at 11 fps plus a 4-cell tail of the cells it just left.
Hit: hit pose + inverse video for ~140 ms and a one-cell knock-back; a one-frame █ block marks the impact cell.
Blinks are hard steps (no fades): cursors 1.06 s period, collectibles 1 frame in 5 at 3 fps, i-frame blink at 16 Hz, glow-up colour swap at 12 Hz.
UI never tweens: transitions none, every blink uses steps(1).
do: Snap every glyph to the cell grid (floor(x / 6), floor(y / 10)) and draw at whole display pixels.
Bake glyphs once into an atlas keyed by glyph + colour + mode and blit cells; bake multi-cell sprites once per cell size.
Put an opaque plate behind every figure, prop and collectible cell so it erases the ground underneath.
Keep the ground dim and sparse (≤ 50 % filled, ≤ #2a994b) so the bright, glowing figures carry the picture.
Draw block, shade and box glyphs procedurally so they tile without gaps at any cell size.
Use inverse video for flashes, scrambling glyphs for damage, typed-out text for messages.
Choose glyphs by silhouette: half blocks for round masses, slashes for limbs, brackets for shells.
Give every state its own glyph pose (walk, breathe, blink, crouch, lunge, hurt, hit) and hold it – motion is a sequence of held text frames.
dont: No sub-cell positions, rotation or scaling of glyphs – a glyph is either in a cell or not.
No colours outside the phosphor ramps; no amber creatures, no green main character.
No full-screen blur or bloom pass per frame; the glow lives in the baked glyphs.
No drop shadows under figures; no gradients inside cells.
No proportional or rounded fonts in the world; no mixed glyph sizes in one grid.
No dense, bright ground textures – a busy ground swallows the figures.
No alpha fades for decay – step down the colour ramp and the glyph ramp (* + · .) instead.
Don't sprinkle accent glyphs (flowers) evenly – keep them in small beds and leave calm, sparse areas.
performance: Very cheap per frame: with 60–120 figures plus particles the drawing code takes ~1–2 ms per frame (median) in headless Chromium. On the first frame at a new cell size a warm-up bakes the ~600 common glyph slots (bursts, digits, scramble set, ramps) into 8 × 8-slot atlas pages and all figure states (≈ 160 sprites: 16 main-character poses in 3 palettes, 6 + 6 critter poses, 5 brute poses, normal and inverse), so later frames never bake; rare extra slots are added on first use. Atlas pages and sprites live in CPU-backed canvases (willReadFrequently) that are only ever drawImage sources. Ground chunks (40 × 24 cells) are generated with a generator in row batches and cached; chunks built before the web font arrived are repainted in place a few per frame. Per frame: one drawImage per figure/prop, one per particle glyph, a few hundred water-crest cells, a scanline pattern fill and one cached vignette canvas. The only full-screen copy is the row tearing, and only during impacts.
